title: Drinking water public notification practice questions
description: Free drinking water public notification practice questions on 40 CFR 141 Subpart Q. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule it comes from.

questions.question: Under 141.201(a), which public water systems must give public notice for NPDWR violations and the other situations in Table 1?

options.A: Only community water systems
options.B: Community, non-transient non-community, and transient non-community water systems
options.C: Only community and non-transient non-community water systems
options.D: Only systems serving 10,000 or more persons

questions.explanation: 141.201(a) applies to "Each owner or operator of a public water system (community water systems, non-transient non-community water systems, and transient non-community water systems)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.201, General public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each owner or operator of a public water system (community water systems, non-transient non-community water systems, and transient non-community water systems) must give notice

questions.question: A system that sells water to a consecutive system has a violation. Under 141.201(c)(1), to whom does the selling system give the public notice?

options.A: Directly to every customer of the consecutive system, with no notice to its owner or operator
options.B: Only to the EPA Administrator
options.C: Only to the State public health officer
options.D: The owner or operator of the consecutive system, which then notifies the persons it serves

questions.explanation: Selling systems "are required to give public notice to the owner or operator of the consecutive system; the consecutive system is responsible for providing public notice to the persons it serves."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.201, General public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: are required to give public notice to the owner or operator of the consecutive system; the consecutive system is responsible for providing public notice to the persons it serves

questions.question: A violation occurs in a hydraulically isolated part of a distribution system. What does 141.201(c)(2) say about limiting the notice to the persons served by that part?

options.A: The primacy agency may allow it, and the permission must be granted in writing
options.B: The system may limit the notice on its own without asking anyone
options.C: Limiting the notice is never allowed
options.D: The system may limit it only for Tier 1 notices

questions.explanation: "The primacy agency may allow the system to limit distribution of the public notice to only persons served by that portion of the system which is out of compliance. Permission by the primacy agency for limiting distribution of the notice must be granted in writing."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.201, General public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Permission by the primacy agency for limiting distribution of the notice must be granted in writing.

questions.question: How does Table 2 to 141.201 define the violations and situations that require a Tier 1 public notice?

options.A: All NPDWR violations not included in any other tier
options.B: Those with potential to have serious adverse effects on human health after many years of exposure
options.C: Those with significant potential to have serious adverse effects on human health as a result of short-term exposure
options.D: Only monitoring and testing procedure violations

questions.explanation: Tier 1 is "required for NPDWR violations and situations with significant potential to have serious adverse effects on human health as a result of short-term exposure."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.201, General public notification requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: required for NPDWR violations and situations with significant potential to have serious adverse effects on human health as a result of short-term exposure

questions.question: Endnote 1 to Appendix A uses failure to prepare Consumer Confidence Reports as an example of a violation not listed in the table. What does it say about notice for such violations?

options.A: They always require a Tier 1 notice
options.B: They always require a Tier 2 notice within 30 days
options.C: They do not require notice, unless otherwise determined by the primacy agency
options.D: They must be reported only to the EPA Administrator

questions.explanation: "Violations and other situations not listed in this table (e.g., failure to prepare Consumer Confidence Reports), do not require notice, unless otherwise determined by the primacy agency."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 141, Appendix A to Subpart Q (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: do not require notice, unless otherwise determined by the primacy agency

questions.question: In Appendix A, the Tier 2 entries for the PFAS MCL violations (Hazard Index PFAS, HFPO-DA, PFHxS, PFNA, PFOA and PFOS) carry an asterisk. What does the asterisk endnote say?

options.A: Beginning April 26, 2029.
options.B: Until March 31, 2016.
options.C: Beginning April 1, 2016.
options.D: Beginning January 1, 2002.

questions.explanation: The PFOA row reads "35. PFOA *2 141.61(c) 3 141.905(c)", and the asterisk endnote reads "* Beginning April 26, 2029."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 141, Appendix A to Subpart Q (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: * Beginning April 26, 2029.

questions.question: What deadline does 141.202(b)(1) set for providing a Tier 1 public notice?

options.A: No later than 30 days after the system learns of the violation
options.B: No later than one year after the system learns of the violation
options.C: With the next Consumer Confidence Report
options.D: As soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation or situation

questions.explanation: Systems must "Provide a public notice as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation or situation requiring Tier 1 public notice".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.202, Tier 1 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Provide a public notice as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation or situation requiring Tier 1 public notice

questions.question: Which situation is listed in Table 1 to 141.202 as requiring a Tier 1 public notice?

options.A: Exceedance of the fluoride secondary maximum contaminant level
options.B: Detection of E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage in source water samples under 141.402(a) and (b)
options.C: Availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring results
options.D: Operation under a variance or an exemption

questions.explanation: Table 1 to 141.202 lists "Detection of E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage in source water samples as specified in § 141.402(a) and § 141.402(b)"; the other three are Tier 3 situations under 141.204.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.202, Tier 1 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Detection of E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage in source water samples as specified in § 141.402(a) and § 141.402(b)

questions.question: Which form of delivery is named in the list in 141.202(c) for Tier 1 notices?

options.A: Hand delivery of the notice to persons served by the water system
options.B: Inclusion in the next Consumer Confidence Report
options.C: An annual report of the previous twelve months' violations
options.D: Mail with the next quarterly water bill

questions.explanation: 141.202(c) lists broadcast media, posting in conspicuous locations, "Hand delivery of the notice to persons served by the water system", or another method approved in writing by the primacy agency.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.202, Tier 1 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Hand delivery of the notice to persons served by the water system

questions.question: Under the current Subpart Q text, amended October 30, 2024 with the lead rule revision (whose revised Subpart I requirements apply by November 1, 2027), which tier does Table 1 to 141.202 assign to an exceedance of the Action Level for lead under 141.80(c)?

options.A: Tier 2
options.B: Tier 1
options.C: Tier 3
options.D: No public notice; only a report to the State

questions.explanation: Table 1 to 141.202, which lists situations requiring a Tier 1 notice, includes "(10) Exceedance of the Action Level for lead as specified in § 141.80(c)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.202, Tier 1 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (10) Exceedance of the Action Level for lead as specified in § 141.80(c).

questions.question: What deadline does 141.203(b)(1) set for the initial Tier 2 public notice, before any primacy agency extension?

options.A: No later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation
options.B: No later than 7 days after the violation is resolved
options.C: No later than one year after the system learns of the violation
options.D: As soon as practical, but no later than 30 days after the system learns of the violation

questions.explanation: "Public water systems must provide the public notice as soon as practical, but no later than 30 days after the system learns of the violation."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.203, Tier 2 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Public water systems must provide the public notice as soon as practical, but no later than 30 days after the system learns of the violation.

questions.question: Unless the primacy agency determines that appropriate circumstances warrant a different frequency, what repeat-notice interval does 141.203(b)(2) set for a Tier 2 violation that persists?

options.A: Every week
options.B: Every two years
options.C: Every three months
options.D: Only once, with no repeat

questions.explanation: "The public water system must repeat the notice every three months as long as the violation or situation persists, unless the primacy agency determines that appropriate circumstances warrant a different repeat notice frequency."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.203, Tier 2 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The public water system must repeat the notice every three months as long as the violation or situation persists

questions.question: A system has a turbidity MCL violation under 141.13(b) and does not consult with the primacy agency within 24 hours. What does 141.203(b)(3) then require?

options.A: Give a Tier 2 notice within 30 days
options.B: Include the violation in the next Consumer Confidence Report
options.C: Wait until the primacy agency makes contact
options.D: Distribute a Tier 1 notice within the next 24 hours (no later than 48 hours after learning of the violation)

questions.explanation: "When consultation does not take place within the 24-hour period, the water system must distribute a Tier 1 notice of the violation within the next 24 hours (i.e., no later than 48 hours after the system learns of the violation)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.203, Tier 2 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When consultation does not take place within the 24-hour period, the water system must distribute a Tier 1 notice of the violation within the next 24 hours

questions.question: Unless the primacy agency directs otherwise in writing, which delivery does 141.203(c)(1)(i) require community water systems to use for a Tier 2 notice?

options.A: Mail or other direct delivery to each customer receiving a bill and to other service connections
options.B: Radio and television broadcast only
options.C: Posting at the treatment plant only
options.D: Publication in the annual Consumer Confidence Report only

questions.explanation: Community water systems must provide notice by "Mail or other direct delivery to each customer receiving a bill and to other service connections to which water is delivered by the public water system", plus other methods to reach other persons regularly served.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.203, Tier 2 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Mail or other direct delivery to each customer receiving a bill and to other service connections to which water is delivered by the public water system

questions.question: Which type of system does 141.204(d) allow to use its Consumer Confidence Report as the vehicle for the initial Tier 3 notice and all repeat notices?

options.A: Transient non-community water systems
options.B: Community water systems
options.C: Non-transient non-community water systems
options.D: Consecutive systems only

questions.explanation: "For community water systems, the Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) required under Subpart O of this part may be used as a vehicle for the initial Tier 3 public notice and all required repeat notices", if the listed conditions are met.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.204, Tier 3 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For community water systems, the Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) required under Subpart O of this part may be used as a vehicle for the initial Tier 3 public notice and all required repeat notices

questions.question: Which violation is listed in Table 1 to 141.204 as requiring a Tier 3 public notice?

options.A: Violation of the MCL for E. coli
options.B: Violation of the MCL for nitrate
options.C: Reporting and recordkeeping violations under Subpart Y
options.D: Failure to comply with the terms and conditions of a variance or exemption in place

questions.explanation: Table 1 to 141.204 lists "Reporting and Recordkeeping violations under subpart Y of 40 CFR part 141." The E. coli and nitrate MCL violations are Tier 1, and failure to comply with variance terms is Tier 2.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.204, Tier 3 Public Notice—Form, manner, and frequency of notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Reporting and Recordkeeping violations under subpart Y of 40 CFR part 141.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the elements 141.205(a) requires in each public notice?

options.A: Whether alternative water supplies should be used
options.B: The certification number of the plant operator
options.C: The names of the customers affected
options.D: The system's annual operating budget

questions.explanation: 141.205(a)(5) requires "Whether alternative water supplies should be used".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.205, Content of the public notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (5) Whether alternative water supplies should be used;

questions.question: For a system serving a large proportion of non-English speaking consumers, as determined by the primacy agency, what does 141.205(c)(2)(i) require the notice to contain?

options.A: A complete translation into every language spoken in the service area
options.B: Nothing beyond the English text
options.C: Information in the appropriate language(s) on the importance of the notice, or a telephone number or address to get a translated copy or assistance
options.D: A statement that translations are not available

questions.explanation: The notice "must contain information in the appropriate language(s) regarding the importance of the notice or contain a telephone number or address where persons served may contact the water system to obtain a translated copy of the notice or to request assistance in the appropriate language."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.205, Content of the public notice (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Special notices and the primacy agency
questions.question: Which systems does 141.208(a) require to give the special notice for fluoride?

options.A: Any public water system that exceeds the fluoride MCL of 4 mg/l
options.B: Transient non-community water systems that exceed 2 mg/l
options.C: Community water systems with any detectable fluoride
options.D: Community water systems that exceed the fluoride SMCL of 2 mg/l but do not exceed the fluoride MCL of 4 mg/l

questions.explanation: "Community water systems that exceed the fluoride secondary maximum contaminant level (SMCL) of 2 mg/l as specified in § 143.3 ... but do not exceed the maximum contaminant level (MCL) of 4 mg/l for fluoride" must give this notice.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.208, Special notice for exceedance of the SMCL for fluoride (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Community water systems that exceed the fluoride secondary maximum contaminant level (SMCL) of 2 mg/l as specified in § 143.3

questions.topic: Special notices and the primacy agency
questions.question: A non-community water system has primacy agency permission under 141.11(d) to exceed the nitrate MCL. What does 141.209(b) require it to do?

options.A: Nothing, because the exceedance is permitted
options.B: Continuously post the fact that nitrate levels exceed 10 mg/l and the potential health effects of exposure
options.C: Include the exceedance only in an annual report
options.D: Notify only the primacy agency each quarter

questions.explanation: Such systems "must provide continuous posting of the fact that nitrate levels exceed 10 mg/l and the potential health effects of exposure", following Tier 1 delivery under 141.202(c).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.209, Special notice for nitrate exceedances above MCL by non-community water systems (NCWS), where granted permission by the primacy agency under § 141.11(d) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: must provide continuous posting of the fact that nitrate levels exceed 10 mg/l and the potential health effects of exposure
